decision: Follow OpenCode for the wire, as the owner directed. The shared public client is permitted; Mercury sends its own User-Agent and referrer, never another product's identity.

facts.fact: All three clients share public client b1a00492-073a-47ea-816f-4c329264a828. OpenCode explicitly calls it public; OpenClaw explicitly calls it shared, warning that consent can say Grok Build.

RFC 8628 device flow, no callback or client secret: POST https://auth.x.ai/oauth2/device/code, then POST https://auth.x.ai/oauth2/token with client_id, device_code and grant_type urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code. Browser authorize endpoint exists but is not this flow.

Form-encoded requests; scope openid profile email offline_access grok-cli:access api:access. Device reply carries device_code, user_code, verification_uri, optional verification_uri_complete, expires_in and interval. authorization_pending waits; slow_down increases delay at least five seconds; access_denied, authorization_denied and expired_token terminate.

Refresh uses the same token endpoint, form grant_type=refresh_token with refresh_token and client_id, no secret. Access expiry is expires_in when stated, otherwise JWT exp is an observed hint; no fixed token lifetime is guaranteed. OpenCode defaults missing expires_in to one hour but Mercury does not treat that as a provider fact.

OpenCode leaves its SDK base at https://api.x.ai/v1 and injects Authorization: Bearer <access token>. Observed live 2026-10-01: that base bills the account's purchased credits per token and refuses the subscription bearer with HTTP 403 personal-team-blocked:spending-limit while no credits are loaded, so it is not the subscription's road. Mercury subscription turns use /responses on the Grok proxy base, its own User-Agent, flat function tools (no defer_loading, no tool-search type) and stateless replay. API keys retain their existing chat road on api.x.ai.

Model access must be read using the selected credential; no verified account model inventory is available without sign-in. Mercury uses GET /v1/models on the credential's own base (the Grok proxy for a subscription, api.x.ai for a key) and never seeds a subscription-only model list from the other clients' defaults.

OpenClaw's OAuth Responses and /models ride https://cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1; inference adds X-XAI-Token-Auth: xai-grok-cli, x-grok-client-version and x-grok-model-override (the model id). Mercury sends exactly these three on the proxy's Responses road and nothing extra on its /models GET; neither ever rides api.x.ai. Tool outputs on the proxy are strings; an image-bearing tool result is flattened and its images re-homed into one user message after the paired outputs, as OpenClaw does.

OpenClaw reads GET https://cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1/billing?format=credits with bearer, x-grok-client-mode=cli and x-grok-client-version=1.0.4. It reads subscription_tier, config.creditUsagePercent, currentPeriod.type/start/end, legacy used/monthlyLimit; explicit zero is a fact, omitted percent is not zero. Prepaid balance is separate; onDemand counters are not included subscription quota. Mercury reads the same endpoint with the same headers for the Grok subscription's included pool (creditUsagePercent as the window's used percent, currentPeriod.end as its reset, prepaidBalance.val cents as the purchased-credits line, subscription_tier as the tier when present) and shows it where every other family's pool shows.

No subscription-specific 429 body or plan claim is established for the proxy road in these sources. Mercury keeps ordinary HTTP 429 / Retry-After handling; an unreadable pool stays an honest reader note, never a fabricated window, tier or balance.

xAI announces SuperGrok or X Premium sign-in for OpenClaw on every tier and describes headless device codes; Hermes warns of backend tier eligibility refusals despite successful browser login. A login is not proof that inference is admitted.
